name: xcode-i18n
description: Visual editor for Xcode String Catalogs (.xcstrings) and legacy .strings — localize iOS, iPadOS & macOS apps in VS Code with a spreadsheet grid, clean git diffs, and translation progress.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No localizations found in this workspace.

This view lists .xcstrings String Catalogs and legacy <lang>.lproj/*.strings files. Open a folder that contains them to see languages and translation progress here.

enumDescriptions: Tighter rows so more fit on screen.
xcodeI18n.displayMode.description: Row density for the String Catalog grid.

xcodeI18n.mergeKeySource.description: Merge the Key and source columns into one. The key shows as a secondary line only when it differs from the source value. Uncheck to show Key and source as separate columns.

xcodeI18n.doubleClickToEdit.description: Require a double-click to open a cell for editing; a single click only selects it. Uncheck to open the editor with a single click.

xcodeI18n.showCommentColumn.description: Show the Comment column — the developer note for each key, in its own column the way Xcode shows it. When off, the note appears under the key instead.

xcodeI18n.showStateColumn.description: Show the State column: a green check when a string is translated, an orange NEW square when it isn't, and a label for every other state. It reports on the first target language shown.

xcodeI18n.allowRemovingManagedStrings.description: Allow deleting keys that Xcode manages automatically. Off by default: such a key is extracted from your source code, so deleting it here only postpones it until the next build. Keys added by hand can always be deleted.

xcodeI18n.validateIcuMessages.markdownDescription: Parse values containing `{` or `}` as ICU MessageFormat: highlight their structure in the grid and flag the syntax errors that would throw at format time (an unbalanced brace, a `plural` with no `other` branch, an unknown branch name), plus placeholders a translation dropped or invented. Turn off if your strings use braces as literal text.

xcodeI18n.catalogFilePatterns.markdownDescription: File name patterns opened as String Catalogs, e.g. `*.strings.json`. Each pattern is registered in `#workbench.editorAssociations#` (globally) so this grid is the default editor for it, with matching `git:` / `gitlens:` entries that keep diffs on the plain-text editor. Removing a pattern here removes its associations again; associations you wrote by hand are left alone.

xcodeI18n.sourceFilePatterns.markdownDescription: File name patterns counted as source code by **Find in code** and **Find unused keys**. A key is looked for as a quoted string literal in double, single or backtick quotes, so `Text("Save")`, `NSLocalizedString("Save", …)`, `t('save')` and `` i18n(`save`) `` all count. Add `*.kt`, `*.py`, `*.vue` or anything else you keep call sites in; vendor folders (`node_modules`, `Pods`, `build`, `DerivedData`, …) are always skipped.

xcodeI18n.translationFunctions.markdownDescription: Function names treated as localization calls when extracting strings. A call whose first argument is a string literal — `t("key", …)`, `i18n("key")` — contributes that key. Member calls match on their last segment, so `t` also covers `i18n.t("key")`. Short names like `t` only work because gitignored build output is never scanned; a checked-in minified bundle would still confuse them.

xcodeI18n.extractionRoot.markdownDescription: Where to look for strings to extract, relative to the catalog file's own folder. The default `..` keeps a sweep inside the module that owns the catalog — `client/lang/messages.xcstrings` scans `client/`, not the whole workspace. Use `../..` to widen it, or `.` to scan only the catalog's folder.

xcodeI18n.autoMarkNeedsReview.markdownDescription: Flag translations as **needs review** when the source they were made from changes — either you edit a source string in the grid, or a sync finds that a string's text or its plural / device variations moved since your last commit. Only settled translations are flagged; empty ones stay `new` and ones already flagged are left alone.

xcodeI18n.markMissingKeysStale.markdownDescription: When syncing, mark previously extracted keys that no longer appear in your code as `stale`. Nothing is deleted — a stale key keeps its translations, and the **−** button can then remove it once it has none. Hand-added (`manual`) and `migrated` keys are never re-filed.

xcodeI18n.excludePatterns.markdownDescription: Files and folders never scanned. **Gitignored files are already skipped**, which is what keeps build output such as `dist/` — where minified code makes every one-letter local look like a `t("…")` call — out of extraction and usage counts; `node_modules` and `.git` are named only to avoid walking a large tree just to discard it. Tests are named because they are *not* gitignored: a string in a test is an assertion about the app rather than part of it, so extracting from one invents entries nobody ships, and counting one as a reference would keep a dead key alive long after the feature was deleted.

xcodeI18n.languageNames.markdownDescription: Display names for language tags VS Code doesn't recognise, e.g. `{ "en-Pseudo": "English (Pseudo)" }`. Everything else keeps its standard name.

scripts.install-local: npm version patch --no-git-tag-version && npm run package && code --install-extension xcode-i18n.vsix --force
